name: Poll Any Job Status Until Complete Using Do...While

parameters.content:
## Poll Any Job Status Until Complete

This workflow keeps checking a job status until it reports as done, then continues.

A real-world example: you trigger a video export, a report generation, or an AI task in an external service. Those operations take time. Instead of waiting a fixed amount, this workflow keeps checking and continues the moment the job is ready.

**How to adapt this for your use case:**
Replace the "Check Job Status" Code node with an HTTP Request node pointing to your API status endpoint. Make sure the response contains a field you can check in the Do...While condition.

For example, if your API returns `{ "state": "complete" }` change the condition to:
`={{ $json.state === 'complete' }}`

## Do...While Node

**Condition:** `$json.status === 'done'`
Checked after every iteration. When true, items exit via Condition Met.

**Wait:** 1 second between each check.
Increase this when polling slow APIs to avoid hammering the endpoint.

**Max Iterations:** 10
If the job never finishes, items exit here with `_loop.timedOut = true` instead of looping forever.

**Condition Met pin** goes to Process Result.
**Loop pin** goes to Check Job Status and back.

## Check Job Status

This is a simulation. Replace it with an HTTP Request node calling your API status endpoint.

The node must return a JSON object containing the field your condition checks. In this example that field is `status`.

The counter and status fields are passed back into Do...While on each iteration so the loop has fresh data to evaluate.

## Process Result

By the time items reach here the loop has finished.

Check `_loop.timedOut` to know whether the job completed or the loop hit max iterations:

- `timedOut: false` means the condition was met. Continue normally.
- `timedOut: true` means the job never finished in time. Handle this separately.

Add an IF node after this to branch based on `$json.timedOut`.
